My kids also liked the food. The location of the property is nice, but the parking is limited, however, there are some private parking lots around the area, that are usually $5–$7. Definitely will be back!

text.text:
Surawon Tofu House is one of those rare spots that feels like a true hidden gem the moment you sit down. It’s unpretentious, comforting, and absolutely packed with flavor. If you’re craving authentic Korean comfort food, this place delivers in every way.

The soon tofu is the star—rich, silky, and deeply satisfying, with that perfect balance of spice and warmth that hits you right away. Their broths taste like they’ve been simmering all day, and every bowl comes out piping hot and full of depth. The banchan is fresh, generous, and constantly refilled, which always makes the meal feel even more welcoming.

Service is friendly and efficient, and the whole experience has that home-style vibe that makes you want to come back regularly. It’s the kind of restaurant where you can bring friends, family, or just treat yourself to a comforting solo meal.

If you’re anywhere near the area, Surawon Tofu House is absolutely worth the stop—a cozy, flavorful, and consistently delicious Korean spot that never disappoints.

I am a loyal customer to Mountain San!!

I’m met the owner and gotten close to most of the servers old and new. I love coming in and knowing that the service is going to be great, music will be playing and the quality of meat is Top Notch!! This is truly a local spot that I was told has Soups and a cold noodles aside from their BBQ (stone & grill).

This is a restaurant that the servers cook for you. The banchon (side dishes) are always great like the salad and onion salad.

I have been going to Mountain San for almost 2 years now and I’ve seen it from when the menu prices for a value BBQ combo was $89.99 now being between $99.99 for 2 people or $109.99-$199.99 depending on the size of the group!!

I celebrated my birthday here and had the best time. Friday & Saturday evenings are the best vibes. Can get busy fast so you may have to wait a while. They have all the flavored soju, makgeolli & Korean beers which are a huge plus.

My photos go back from a week ago to the first time I went to Mountain San. I love bringing my friends here that are visiting LA!

Parking is free with validation for up to 3 hours. It’s located in a shopping center which is super convenient. Drive up to the 3rd/4th level where there is a sign for the restaurant.

text.text:
My second time at Gol Tong and honestly it's even better than the first time. It is a popular spot and expect to wait since it is a one man shop. The owner used to be a director and he is the chef, server and host. The place is uniquely decorated with posters and multiple TV screens, which is super entertaining.

We ordered the popular Director's Cut Edition Half and Half which is half soy garlic and chili flavor. When we received our tray in a timely manner and it's an overflowing plate! The fried chicken is divided in half so you can see the two flavors well, served with a fruit dipping sauce and the most seasonal fruit you'll have ever seen on one plate. This is not your typical Korean fried chicken spot, but all the fruit works well since the tangy and tartiness mixes well with the fried chicken. The chicken is tender on the inside and fried well despite all the sauce. There must have been at least 12+ different seasonal fruits such as raspberries, pineapples, mangoes, strawberries, blueberries, avocado, grapes, bananas, kiwis, plums, nectarines, korean pear, peppers and more! I love how the fruits are sliced and placed expertly around the whole dish. It's so aesthetically pleasing. I love how it all works together!

I absolutely love how friendly the owner is and he always has such a big smile on his face. The place is on the smaller side with about 5 tables, so expect a wait if it is busy. There is a self-service for pop and water, and there are plates, utensils and napkins on the side for when you are eating. There's also some gloves too, which I highly recommend using when you are eating. Do not skip out on Gol Tong Chicken and try out this innovative way of using fruit with korean fried chicken!

It is a solid, reliable spot for the sides, but the mains could use a boost to be truly memorable.

If you are looking for a clean, upscale, and genuinely delicious Korean BBQ experience, look no further. I will definitely be back very soon!

text.text: Wow I can’t believe how incredible the food is here. This is not your typical Korean bbq. This is elevated and intentional Korean food with impeccable, full table service. I tried the $185 combo today and added a $12 nengmyun. Keep in mind it’s Pyeongyang style nengmyun and is different than what you may think is “standard” nengmyun. The meat quality is fantastic here. Really nice marbling. The standout for me was the galbi. So tender and struck a nice balance between the soy and the sweetness for me. The ssam and banchan are also so beautifully presented. The soups at kbbq tend to be an afterthought type of filler dish, but they don’t do regular soups here. The doenjang jjigae was made like my grandma makes, with a deep, umami anchovy based broth. They even utilized shiitake mushroom in it, which I have never seen before. Definitely an additional umami flavor to the dish, but this is really what I mean by everything is intentional. The spicy beef rib soup is my recommendation for the soup for the combo. It’s like the best yukgaejang/galbitang crossover I’ve ever had. The clean aftertaste from the radish in it is fantastic. The flavors of the different ingredients used really stood out to me. The nengmyun broth had a deep beef flavor and touch of sweetness that was simply perfect once I added in mustard and vinegar. The noodles are not my personal preference (I like hamheung style), but the broth is just *wow*. I was quite impressed to say the least. The meal combo was enough for 3 of us. They began to really fill up around 6:30. I can’t recommend this place enough.

It is incredibly disheartening to experience such a disgusting attitude, especially when introducing new customers to a place I genuinely love. The kitchen staff deserves five stars for always delivering incredible food, but management seriously needs to address this server's behavior, as excellent food deserves matching service.

text.text:
My sister and I visited Lu’s Cafe for the first time on a Sunday around 11:30 a.m. to celebrate something for her. Since we chose it largely because of the strong reviews, I hoped it would live up to the hype. It ended up exceeding both of our expectations.

There was already a line when we arrived, and it came and went throughout our visit, so the café is clearly popular. On such a hot, sunny day, the two large standing umbrellas outside also provided some welcome shade near the waiting area.

The space itself was almost worth the visit. It is fairly small and modest from the outside, but they have used it impressively. The design is minimalist without feeling bare, with jade-colored wall accents, Chinese-language signage, warm hanging lights, arched details, barrel-style seating, and vintage travel images of Shanghai and other parts of China. Even the small table of regional cookbooks outside the restroom felt thoughtful rather than staged.

We ordered the peanut sauce noodles, a chicken rice bowl, Hong Kong-style French toast, and two milk teas. Everything arrived surprisingly quickly despite how busy the café was. The French toast was probably my favorite: crisp outside and soft and fluffy inside. The chicken rice bowl was also excellent, with subtle, balanced flavors that were not overly salty. The noodles were good, although the peanut flavor was a little stronger than I personally prefer, while both milk teas were flavorful without being too sweet. Overall, the food showed a real sense of balance rather than relying on excess salt, sugar, or heaviness.

Our total came to around $50 for two people, including tip, which felt like very good value for Los Angeles.

The café is largely self-service. Staff bring the food to your table, while water, napkins, and other basics are available for guests to get themselves. Still, everything was straightforward, the food came quickly, and the staff were pleasant and accommodating. Before we ordered, the woman at the counter also asked whether either of us had any food allergies. Since my girlfriend has celiac disease, I noticed and appreciated that. I cannot speak to what gluten-free or allergy accommodations they actually offer, but it was reassuring that they asked.

There is only one all-gender restroom, so there was occasionally a short wait. However, it was reasonably well maintained considering how busy the restaurant was, and the kitchen area I could see also appeared clean and organized.

Both my sister and I have traveled in Hong Kong and Taiwan. I am Korean American, so I would not claim to be the final authority on authenticity, but the food and atmosphere felt genuinely inspired by the region rather than merely themed around it. The largely Asian crowd during our visit also suggested that Lu’s has built a strong local following.

My sister is an excellent cook, a discerning eater, and someone who has traveled extensively, so I was especially curious about her reaction. She gave the whole experience an enthusiastic thumbs-up and said she would happily return. Since we were there for a small celebration, I was glad the café felt special enough for the occasion.

Parking is the only real inconvenience, since street parking in Koreatown can be difficult, but that is more of a neighborhood issue than a criticism of the café itself.

Lu’s delivered fast, well-balanced food, thoughtful design, good value, and an experience that felt both relaxed and memorable. We went in hoping it would match its reputation and left pleasantly surprised that it exceeded it.

text.text: Got a recommendation for brunch at OpenAire on the 2nd floor pool deck (& converted greenhouse) of the Line Hotel near  downtown LA.  For a Sunday morning, it was less busy than I expected, but starting filling up as we were getting ready to leave (post-church crowd?)  Cool menu, interesting twists on old favorites, servers were all chill and helpful.  The execution of the menu was very good - we didn't put a mediocre bite in our mouths.  The Panna Cotta that I insisted on ordering, even though I was kind of full, was the perfect cap to the meal.  The hotel itself seems like it needs a refresh, and having this glass-ceiling, plant-filled space right next to the hotel pool was a little quirky, but the service and meal were excellent.  Would recommend strongly.

Joo Pocha – The Ultimate KBBQ + Karaoke Spot! 🎤🔥

If you’re looking for a fun, authentic Korean night out, Joo Pocha is THE place to be! Located in LA’s K-town, this spot serves up delicious Korean comfort food AND has an NRB (노래방/karaoke) right next door—so you can eat, drink, and sing your heart out all in one place! 🎶🍻

What we had:

🍖 NEW Thinly-Sliced Frozen Pork Belly – A Korean favorite that’s trending right now!

Pro tip: Since it’s super thin, cook it slowly on medium heat to get the perfect crispy bite!

🐙 Spicy Stir-Fried Baby Octopus – My favorite dish of the night! 🌶🔥 It’s insanely spicy—I got the hottest level, and even my spice-loving friend struggled with Level 2. Adjust your heat level accordingly!

✨ Why You Should Check It Out:

✔ Authentic Korean pocha vibes – It truly feels like a night out in Seoul!
✔ NRB (karaoke) is connected – No need to move to another location after dinner! 🎤
✔ Great spot for groups – Food, drinks, and karaoke? A perfect combo for a fun night!

⭐ Overall Rating: 9/10
🔥 Must-Try: Spicy Stir-Fried Baby Octopus & Thinly-Sliced Pork Belly
🚗 Parking: Free lot in the back (also the entrance!)

Would I go again? 100% YES. Whether you’re craving delicious Korean bar food or looking for a one-stop spot for dinner + karaoke, Joo Pocha is a must-visit!
